title: ripng for ipv6
abstract: this document describes ripng, an extension of the routing information protocol (rip) designed for use with ipv6 networks. ripng is a distance-vector routing protocol that uses hop count as its metric.

section content.introduction: ripng is an extension of rip designed to operate with ipv6 networks. it uses the same distance-vector algorithm as rip but is modified to accommodate ipv6 addressing and packet formats.
section content.ripng message format: ripng messages consist of a header and one or more route tables, each containing a set of route table entries (rtes). the header includes fields for version, command, and other control information.
section content.ripng message transmission: ripng messages are transmitted using udp as the transport protocol. each ripng message is sent as a udp datagram to port 521.
section content.control functions: ripng includes optional administrative controls such as neighbor lists and destination filters to restrict routing updates based on network policy or security considerations.
section content.security considerations: ripng relies on ipv6 security mechanisms like the ip authentication header and the ip encapsulating security payload for secure routing information exchanges.
